items.issue: The symbol d is undefined. If read as head_dim, the formula omits the number of attention heads. The standard full-attention forward-pass term is ~4·n_layers·L²·d_model, where d_model = n_heads × d_head, counting both QK^T and AV matmuls.

items.fix_instruction: Define d at first use as the model hidden dimension (d = n_heads × d_head = 8192 here), state the term counts both QK^T and AV for full dense attention, and note it excludes projections and softmax.
items.evidence: chapter-08.md §1 first paragraph: 'attention adds a term quadratic in context length (~4·n_layers·L²·d, §1 below)'. Regex search of chapter-08 for 'd =', 'where d', 'd denotes', 'd is defined', 'd_model' finds no definition of d; the canonical scenario states '80-layer, hidden-8192' and the worked table uses the value explicitly ('1.288 + 4 ×80 ×9,200² ×8,192'), so d = 8192 = hidden dimension is only implicit — a reader can misread d as head_dim (which would drop the n_heads factor).

items.issue: Tensor cores are compute units, not memory-hierarchy levels; GPU interconnect and other GPUs are communication resources, not memory-capacity levels. The caption later says 'compute, memory and interconnect are separate groups within this stack, not levels of one ladder', which contradicts the single 'resource stack' ordering that places tensor cores between registers and SRAM.
items.quoted_clause: The resource stack runs from the smallest/fastest/closest resource (registers, tensor cores, on-chip SRAM) to the largest/slower/farther (HBM, GPU interconnect, other GPUs).
items.fix_instruction: Restructure figure and caption into separate groups (compute units / memory hierarchy / interconnect); if a ladder remains, restrict it to the memory hierarchy and stop calling the combined set one ladder.
items.evidence: chapter-08.md Fig 8.1 caption: 'The resource stack runs from the smallest/fastest/closest resource (registers, tensor cores, on-chip SRAM) to the largest/slower/farther (HBM, GPU interconnect, other GPUs).' Same caption: 'compute, memory and interconnect are separate groups within this stack, not levels of one ladder.' Follow-up paragraph: 'Read this ladder together with the roofline:'. items.issue: The same paragraph says 'keeping data on-chip raises that intensity'. Arithmetic intensity depends on data reuse and tiling, including how much data the kernel keeps on-chip. Saying the horizontal position is 'not by where the work sits' contradicts the locality effect.

items.fix_instruction: Rewrite: 'the horizontal position is set by arithmetic intensity, which depends on the kernel's data reuse and tiling — including how much data it keeps on-chip — not merely on the nominal memory level.'
items.evidence: chapter-08.md: 'a kernel's horizontal position (FLOP/byte) is set by its arithmetic intensity — not by where the work sits on this resource stack.' The flat denial conflicts with both follow-ons in the same paragraph.

items.issue: FLOPs is a quantity of work, not a rate. The intended meaning is 'adding more compute throughput (FLOP/s)' or 'adding more compute capacity'. As written, 'adding more FLOPs' could mean doing more operations, which is not the roofline point.

items.fix_instruction: Replace with 'adding more compute throughput (FLOP/s) won't help' (or 'more compute capacity'); keep FLOPs for work counts.
items.evidence: chapter-08.md §2: 'FLOPs are like the total distance of a trip: they tell us how much work the request requires, not how fast the system can cover it. ... if the arithmetic intensity is below the ridge, adding more FLOPs won't help because we are waiting for data.' The same paragraph defines FLOPs as work; the book uses TFLOPS/FLOP/s for rates ('989 TFLOPS', '346 TFLOPS'). 'Adding more FLOPs' literally means more work, not more compute throughput — terminology drift confirmed.

items.page_hint: Chapter 9 §5, Common Mistakes, first bullet, parenthetical
items.issue: The statement is true only per phase, not for the whole all-reduce. Total per-link traffic in a ring all-reduce is 2(N−1)/N of the tensor. For N=2, the per-phase fraction is 1/2, but the total per-link traffic is one full tensor, which is why the preceding sentence says a two-rank collective can saturate the link. As written, the parenthetical appears to contradict that sentence.
items.quoted_clause: and by the ring model of §9.3 each link still carries (N−1)/N of the tensor.
items.fix_instruction: chapter-09.md L136: change the parenthetical to 'per phase each link carries (N−1)/N of the tensor; over the full reduce-scatter plus all-gather each link carries 2(N−1)/N — for N=2 that totals one full tensor per link, which is why a two-rank collective can saturate the link.'
items.evidence: Quote found verbatim: chapter-09.md L136 'and by the ring model of §9.3 each link still carries (N−1)/N of the tensor.' §9.3 states the scope the parenthetical omits — chapter-09.md L90: 'Each phase sends (N-1)M/N=122.5 GB per rank; reduce-scatter followed by all-gather therefore sends 245 GB' — so per-link total is 2(N−1)/N (245 GB = 2x122.5 for N=8, M=140). For N=2 the unqualified parenthetical reads 1/2 while total per-link traffic is one full tensor, which is what the preceding clause ('A two-rank collective over one path ... can saturate the link') relies on. The factor of 2 and the per-phase qualifier are genuinely absent from the parenthetical.
